question: How did the gift of a splendid scarlet dressing gown end up costing Denis Diderot his whole study?
answer: It made everything else look shabby. In his essay on parting with his old dressing gown, Diderot replaced his straw chair, his desk, his wall hangings, one by one, to match the new robe. The old gown had fitted his life; the new one demanded a new life to fit it.
move: One upgrade can quietly raise the standard for everything around it.
ask: What did my last new purchase make me want to replace next?
reference: McCracken, Culture and Consumption, Indiana University Press, 1988; Diderot, Regrets on Parting with My Old Dressing Gown, 1769
